title: Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program Canada 2026: Free Leadership Training and Paid Placement for Newcomer Women
summary: The Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program (ALP) is a free leadership and skills development opportunity designed to support racialized newcomer women in Canada with professional development, employment readiness, career coaching and experiential learning opportunities. The program aims to bridge the gap between the skills of newcomer women and the changing needs of employers through intensive training in both soft and technical skills. The Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program combines structured skills development with practical career preparation and wrap-around support. Participants receive training in areas such as leadership, project management, digital fluency, workplace human rights, communication, networking, personal branding and employment readiness. Following the skills development component, participants may also participate in an experiential learning opportunity, which can include paid job placement opportunities. The programme is delivered in partnership with universities, colleges and skills development training partners and is designed specifically around the needs and aspirations of newcomer women seeking greater economic integration, career advancement and leadership development. About the Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program The Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program is a skills and leadership development programme created to help address employment and professional development barriers faced by racialized newcomer women. The programme focuses on helping participants strengthen their professional skills while gaining practical knowledge that can support their transition into the Canadian workforce. Rather than focusing solely on classroom-based learning, the programme combines skills development, employment preparation, coaching and experiential learning. The programme is free for participants . Participants receive: Skills and professional development training Employment readiness support Leadership development Career coaching Mentorship Wrap-around support Practical workplace preparation Opportunities for experiential learning Potential paid job placement opportunities The programme also addresses important aspects of working in the Canadian workplace, including employment human rights, equity, diversity and inclusion, cross-cultural communication and professional communication. Sister2Sister ALP Micro-Credentials The Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program offers two micro-credentials that provide participants with additional professional and technical development. 1. MBA Essentials The MBA Essentials micro-credential is developed by Rotman Executive Education , a division of the Rotman School of Management. The course introduces participants to important business concepts and helps develop strategic thinking and leadership skills that can be applied in today s workplace. The MBA Essentials component includes a six-week asynchronous online course , followed by a four-week guided capstone project . Participants explore areas such as: Strategy Finance Marketing Operations Leadership Data-driven decision-making Communicating business value Cross-functional collaboration The course is led by expert faculty from Rotman and uses content grounded in real-world business challenges. The capstone component gives participants an opportunity to apply what they have learned to a practical challenge. 2. Digital Fluency in the Workforce The second micro-credential is Digital Fluency in the Workforce , delivered through Humber College. This micro-credential focuses on the digital competencies required by employers across different sectors in Canada. It is a six-week self-paced online course designed to help participants become more confident and effective in professional digital environments. The course covers: Effective use of digital tools Digital communication Safe management of digital information Reliable online research Professional communication Time management Information management Project management using digital tools Evaluation of online sources Creation and presentation of visual data Individual and collaborative digital work Together, the two micro-credentials provide participants with both business knowledge and practical digital competencies. Completing the Sister2Sister Program To graduate from the programme and receive the relevant certificate, participants must complete both micro-credentials. Participation in the skills development component is mandatory. Participants should therefore be prepared to commit consistently to the programme. Missing more than two classes can result in disqualification from the programme. This attendance requirement is important because the programme is structured around continuous professional development and practical skills development. Employment Readiness and Career Development A major component of the Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program is employment readiness. The programme provides participants with practical support designed to help them prepare for career opportunities in Canada. Employment readiness activities can include: Resume development LinkedIn profile building Personal branding Professional networking Interview preparation Behavioural interview training Business writing Professional presentations Self-awareness Emotional intelligence Conflict resolution Team building Cross-cultural communication Participants also receive career coaching and support designed to help them identify their strengths and present themselves effectively to potential employers. The programme provides counselling and professional development services including resume writing, profile building, job interview rehearsals and self-advocacy training. Leadership and Workplace Skills Training The Sister2Sister programme goes beyond traditional employment preparation by developing participants leadership and workplace capabilities. The programme includes training related to leadership, team motivation, stakeholder engagement and communication. Participants can develop skills in: Leadership Team motivation Stakeholder engagement Communication planning Problem-solving Decision-making Managing change Conflict resolution Team building Emotional intelligence Self-awareness The programme also includes education around employment human rights and equity, diversity and inclusion in the Canadian workplace. Technical and Project Management Training Participants receive technical skills development related to project management and workplace processes. The training can cover: Project planning Scope management Requirements definition Risk assessment Quality management Project cost estimation Project monitoring Change control Project close-out processes These skills can be valuable across multiple sectors because project management knowledge is relevant to a wide range of professional roles. Why Join the Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program? The programme offers participants an opportunity to combine professional training with practical career development. Some of the key benefits include: Build a Professional Network Participants join a community of immigrant women who are developing their professional careers and leadership capabilities. This creates opportunities to build meaningful professional relationships and expand networks. Develop Leadership Skills The programme is specifically designed to strengthen leadership capacity among racialized newcomer women. Participants can develop the confidence and skills required to progress professionally and take on greater responsibilities. Gain Professional Micro-Credentials Participants can complete the two micro-credentials offered through the programme, covering MBA Essentials and Digital Fluency in the Workforce. Improve Career Readiness The employment readiness component helps participants strengthen resumes, LinkedIn profiles, interviewing skills, networking abilities and personal branding. Receive Coaching and Mentorship Participants receive career coaching and mentorship as part of the programme s broader support structure. Access Experiential Learning After completing the skills development component, participants may participate in an experiential learning opportunity lasting between four and sixteen weeks. For some participants, this can include paid job placement opportunities. Eligibility Criteria for the Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program The Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program is specifically intended for racialized newcomer women who meet the programme s immigration and participation requirements. Applicants must fall within one of the specified newcomer categories. Eligible groups include racialized immigrant and/or refugee women who arrived in Canada within the last 10 years. This can include: Permanent residents Protected persons Naturalized Canadian citizens who immigrated to Canada within the relevant period Individuals admitted to Canada under a federal emergency or humanitarian measure The programme also accepts certain newcomer women with a Canada-Ukraine Authorization for Emergency Travel (CUAET) , provided they have a 900-series Social Insurance Number (SIN) and an open work permit. Refugee claimants with a 900-series SIN and an open work permit can also qualify. Individuals with a 900-series SIN and an open work permit who have received preliminary federal government approval and are waiting for their permanent residence status to be finalized may also qualify. In addition to the immigration-related criteria, applicants must: Be at least 18 years old. Hold an undergraduate degree or higher. Currently be unemployed. Have proficient English language skills, both written and verbal. Not currently be enrolled in full-time school or training. Reside in Ontario. Be willing and able to commit approximately 10 hours per week to the programme. Be willing and able to participate in both in-person and virtual sessions. Applicants should carefully review these requirements before applying because the programme is specifically designed for the identified newcomer population. Program Duration and Schedule The Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program has several stages. The skills development component lasts 16 weeks . Classes generally take place on Saturdays between approximately 10:00 AM and 4:30 PM . The programme uses a blended learning model, meaning participants may engage through synchronous sessions, asynchronous learning and other delivery formats. Following successful completion of the skills development component, participants may proceed to an experiential learning opportunity. The experiential learning period can last between four and sixteen weeks , depending on the type of opportunity. Some participants may receive paid job placement opportunities through the programme s strategic employer partner network. Program Orientation The programme orientation session is scheduled for: 20 November 2026 Time: 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM Eastern Time Attendance at the orientation session is mandatory . Applicants should therefore ensure that they are available to participate in the orientation if selected. Mode of Delivery The programme uses multiple delivery formats to accommodate different aspects of the training. Training may be delivered: In person Virtually through Zoom Asynchronously The experiential learning component may also be offered in different formats depending on the requirements of participating employers. Experiential learning opportunities may therefore be: In person Hybrid Virtual The exact arrangement can depend on the employer and the nature of the placement. Experiential Learning and Paid Placement Opportunities One of the distinctive features of the Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program is its connection to experiential learning. After completing the skills development training, participants may receive opportunities to apply what they have learned in practical professional environments. The experiential learning period can last from four to sixteen weeks. For some participants, the opportunity can include a paid job placement through the programme s strategic partner network. This practical component is intended to help participants transition from training into real workplace environments and gain experience that can support their future employment. Employer and Strategic Partner Network The programme also works with employer partners who can provide experiential learning and employment opportunities. Participating employers can gain access to a talent pool of trained newcomer women while contributing to immigrant women s economic empowerment and professional advancement. Employer partners can also receive support related to mentoring, internship oversight and participant development. The programme indicates that employers hiring from its talent pool may receive up to 100% of wages, to a maximum of $5,000, for each new hire . This employer incentive is designed to encourage organizations to participate in the programme and create employment opportunities for immigrant women. Support Provided to Participants The Sister2Sister programme takes a broad approach to professional development. In addition to technical and leadership training, participants receive wrap-around support relating to mental, emotional and social well-being. The programme recognizes that successful career integration can require more than technical skills alone. Participants can therefore receive support in areas such as: Career development Employment preparation Counselling Resume development Interview preparation Self-advocacy Career coaching Mentorship Professional networking This combination of skills training and support is intended to help participants build confidence while preparing for career advancement. Application Process Interested applicants should review the eligibility requirements carefully before beginning the application. Applicants should ensure that they can commit to the programme s time requirements and participate in the required training formats. The application process should include reviewing the programme requirements and submitting the required information through the designated application channel. Because participation requires a substantial time commitment, prospective applicants should ensure that they can attend the programme s scheduled sessions and complete both micro-credentials. Applicants should also be prepared to participate in the mandatory orientation session scheduled for November 20, 2026. Important Program Information Before applying, prospective participants should take note of the following: The programme is free for participants. The skills development component lasts 16 weeks. Classes generally take place on Saturdays. Participants are expected to commit approximately 10 hours per week. More than two missed classes can result in disqualification. Both micro-credentials must be completed to graduate. The programme uses in-person, virtual and asynchronous learning. Experiential learning can last between four and sixteen weeks. Some experiential learning opportunities may include paid placements. The mandatory orientation is scheduled for November 20, 2026. The Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program provides a comprehensive opportunity for racialized newcomer women in Ontario to strengthen their leadership, digital, business, project management and employment skills while receiving career coaching, mentorship and broader professional support. Through its two micro-credentials, employment readiness training and experiential learning component, the programme combines education with practical career development. Participants can build professional networks, strengthen their leadership capabilities and prepare for employment opportunities in the Canadian workforce. For eligible newcomer women seeking to improve their professional skills and advance their careers, the Sister2Sister Advanced Leadership Program offers a valuable free leadership and skills development opportunity , with the potential for experiential learning and paid job placement. title: University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme 2027: R250,000 Funding for South African and International Researchers
summary: The University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme 2027 is inviting applications from emerging researchers seeking to advance their academic careers through postdoctoral research at the University of Pretoria (UP) in South Africa. Managed through the University of Pretoria Graduate Support Hub (GSH) under the Department of Research and Innovation (DRI) Postdoctoral Framework, the programme is designed to attract high-calibre emerging scholars, strengthen institutional research capacity, and support research leaders across UP faculties. The Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme 2027 is open to South African citizens, permanent residents and international candidates who meet the programme s academic, age and research requirements. Applicants must generally have obtained their PhD within five years before the application call date and must be aged 40 or younger at the time of submission. For the 2027 call, co-funding is the priority pathway . Under the co-funding arrangement, the Department of Research and Innovation can contribute up to R125,000 per year, while the participating UP host must provide at least R125,000 per year. This creates a fellowship package of at least R250,000 per year. The final application deadline is 30 October 2026 at 23:59 SAST . Late applications will not be accepted. About the University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme 2027 The University of Pretoria s Postdoctoral Framework forms part of the institution s broader efforts to strengthen research excellence and develop the next generation of researchers. The 2027 fellowship programme focuses particularly on attracting talented researchers who are within five years of receiving their doctoral degrees. Through the programme, the University of Pretoria seeks to increase research capacity, support established research leaders and provide emerging scholars with an environment in which they can develop their research portfolios. The programme is managed by the Graduate Support Hub (GSH) in alignment with the strategic priorities of the Department of Research and Innovation. The fellowship has three principal strategic objectives: 1. Talent Attraction The programme seeks to recruit high-calibre emerging scholars from South Africa and internationally. Candidates who have completed their PhD within the specified five-year window can apply to conduct postdoctoral research at the University of Pretoria. 2. Capacity Building The fellowship is intended to strengthen the research impact of the University of Pretoria by supporting research leaders and host academics across the University s faculties. Postdoctoral fellows therefore become part of an academic research environment where their work can contribute to existing research programmes while also allowing them to develop their own research profile. 3. Expansion of Co-Funding A major priority of the 2027 call is the expansion of co-funded fellowships. The co-funding model allows the Department of Research and Innovation and an eligible UP host to jointly finance a postdoctoral fellow. The DRI contribution can reach R125,000 per year, while the host is required to provide at least R125,000 per year. The combined funding must provide a fellowship package of at least R250,000 annually. University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 Funding Options The 2027 programme provides three distinct funding pathways for emerging researchers. Applicants should carefully distinguish between these categories because they have different funding sources, durations and conditions. 1. UP Co-Funded Postdoctoral Fellowship The UP Co-Funding category is the priority pathway for the 2027 call. Under this model: The total fellowship package is at least R250,000 per year . The DRI provides up to R125,000 per year . The UP host provides at least R125,000 per year . The host must have an appropriate funding source. A formal written commitment from the host is required. The host s funding source must be disclosed. An active UP Cost Centre code is required. Co-funded applications receive priority during panel allocations. The co-funding model is therefore particularly important for applicants who already have a suitable UP research leader willing and able to host their research. The call indicates that applications under the co-funding category are reviewed first during panel allocations, with the objective of maximising the number of successful fellowship awards. However, satisfying the co-funding requirement does not automatically guarantee an award. Applicants must still satisfy the University s academic eligibility requirements and pass the relevant merit and institutional review processes. 2. UP PhD Fellow Track The UP PhD Fellow pathway provides a one-year fellowship with a total value of R250,000 . This category is funded entirely through the DRI allocation and is intended to support direct transitions from doctoral studies into postdoctoral research. The duration is: One year Non-extendable Applicants interested in this pathway should therefore understand that it differs from the two-year fellowship categories and should plan their research activities accordingly. 3. UP-Funded Postdoctoral Fellowship The standard UP-Funded pathway provides funding of R250,000 per year . This category is funded through the University s institutional DRI allocation and is highly competitive. The fellowship can run for up to two years, subject to the applicable conditions. For all two-year fellowship categories, continuation into the second year is not automatic. Year-two renewal remains dependent on a formal progress evaluation and the availability of funds. Important Co-Funding Advantage The University of Pretoria has identified co-funding as the principal priority for the 2027 call. The co-funding structure is based on a financial partnership between the Department of Research and Innovation and the UP research host. The structure is: DRI contribution: up to R125,000 per year Host contribution: at least R125,000 per year Minimum combined fellowship package: R250,000 per year The host contribution may exceed R125,000 where additional institutional funding is available. Applicants should note that securing a willing research host is therefore particularly important for the co-funded pathway. Host Commitment Requirements A host seeking to support a co-funded applicant must provide the required institutional commitment. The application requires: Formal written commitment from the UP host. Verification of the funding source. Disclosure of the relevant host funding. An active UP Cost Centre code. The co-funding arrangement does not eliminate the University s academic assessment process. Applicants are still assessed on academic merit, research quality, institutional alignment and other eligibility requirements. Who Can Apply for the University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027? The programme has specific eligibility requirements that all applicants must satisfy. PhD Requirement Applicants must have been awarded their doctoral degree within five years prior to the application call date . This requirement is intended to focus the programme on emerging researchers who are still within the early stages of their postdoctoral academic careers. Applicants should therefore carefully verify the date on which their PhD was formally awarded or conferred. Age Requirement Applicants must be 40 years of age or younger at the time of submission . This is a mandatory eligibility requirement and should be considered before preparing an application. Nationality The fellowship has a global scope. Applications are open to: South African citizens South African permanent residents International candidates International researchers can therefore apply, provided they satisfy the programme s academic, age, research and institutional requirements. Successful international candidates are responsible for obtaining the appropriate South African immigration clearance before arrival and registration. Confirmed University of Pretoria Research Host Applicants must have a committed University of Pretoria Research Leader/Host who endorses the proposed research project. This is a fundamental part of the application because the postdoctoral fellowship is connected to a UP research environment. Applicants should therefore identify an appropriate research leader whose academic expertise and research environment align with the proposed project. Applicants Awaiting Formal PhD Graduation The programme provides a specific procedure for applicants who have completed all PhD requirements but are still waiting for the formal graduation ceremony. Such candidates cannot simply provide a personal declaration that they have completed their doctorate. Instead, they must submit an official institutional letter from the registrar or examination office of the university that awarded the degree. The letter must confirm that: All PhD requirements have been completely fulfilled. The applicant has satisfied the requirements for the doctoral degree. The information is formally verified by the awarding institution. The letter must be issued on official institutional letterhead. Documents That Will Not Be Accepted The following cannot substitute for the required official institutional confirmation: Applicant self-declarations Emails from the university Personal correspondence Personal letters from individual academic supervisors Non-official documentation can result in disqualification. There is also an important timing requirement: the PhD must be formally conferred before the successful fellow s official start date at the University of Pretoria . Applicants who are waiting for graduation should therefore pay particular attention to their university s official degree-conferral process. Application Process for the University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 The application is submitted through an online UP application process. The call outlines a seven-step submission roadmap. Step 1: Select the Fellowship Category Applicants must identify the appropriate funding pathway. The available categories include: UP Co-Funding UP-Funded UP PhD Fellow Because co-funding is the priority for the 2027 call, applicants who are eligible for and able to secure the required host contribution should carefully consider this category. Step 2: Complete Personal and Biographical Information Applicants must provide their personal and biographical details. An active ORCID link is also required. Applicants should ensure that their ORCID information is current and accurately reflects their academic identity and research outputs. Step 3: Provide PhD Information Applicants must provide information about their doctoral qualification, including: Institution where the PhD was obtained PhD award date Relevant doctoral documentation Applicants awaiting formal graduation must follow the special documentation procedure described in the call. Step 4: Provide UP Host Information Applicants must provide information about their University of Pretoria research host. This includes the relevant: Faculty Department Research Leader/Host The host must be appropriately committed to supporting the proposed research. Step 5: Upload Supporting Documents Applicants must upload all required supporting documentation. Incomplete applications are subject to disqualification without assessment. Applicants should therefore prepare and verify all PDF documents before submitting the application. Step 6: Complete the Declaration Applicants must accept the applicable legal terms and declarations associated with the fellowship application. Step 7: Submit the Application The completed application must be submitted by: 30 October 2026 at 23:59 SAST. Early submission is strongly recommended because applicants who wait until the final day may encounter system congestion or technical difficulties. Required Documents for the Postdoctoral Fellowship Application Applicants are expected to provide a comprehensive application dossier. The required documents include: Curriculum Vitae and Publications List Applicants must submit a CV that demonstrates their academic and research experience. The CV should be accompanied by a publications list or research-output record. This is important because the applicant s research track record forms part of the institutional assessment. Certified PhD Certificate Applicants should provide a certified copy of their PhD certificate. Where appropriate, an official institutional completion letter may be submitted in accordance with the special provisions for candidates awaiting formal graduation. Academic Transcripts Certified academic transcripts showing the applicant s academic record are required. Applicants should ensure that their documentation meets the required certification standards. Certified Identification or Passport Applicants must provide a certified copy of an appropriate national identification document or passport. This is particularly relevant for international candidates. Academic Reference The application requires one formal recommendation letter . Applicants should select an academic referee who can provide meaningful evidence of their research ability and academic potential. Research Proposal A research proposal is required and must be a maximum of five pages, excluding references . The proposal is one of the most important components of the application because the proposed research is evaluated for originality, feasibility, contribution and alignment. UP Host CV The curriculum vitae of the University of Pretoria Research Leader/Host must also be provided. This helps demonstrate the research environment and expertise available to support the fellow. Employment Status Declaration Applicants must provide a formal declaration concerning their employment status. Co-Funding Confirmation For co-funded applications, the required host co-funding confirmation must be completed through the designated online Google application form. UP Cost Centre Code Co-funded applications must disclose the relevant host funding source and provide the applicable UP Cost Centre code. Research Proposal Requirements The research proposal should provide a clear and convincing explanation of the proposed postdoctoral research. The five-page proposal should cover several key components. Background, Rationale and Research Problem The proposal should establish the context of the research and clearly explain the problem the project intends to address. Applicants should demonstrate why the research matters and identify the gap or challenge that makes the project necessary. Aims, Objectives and Methodology The proposal should state clear research aims and objectives. It should also explain the methodology that will be used to achieve those objectives. The research approach should be realistic and appropriate to the discipline. Work Plan and Timeline Applicants should provide a realistic work plan showing how the research can be completed within the fellowship period. The timeline should demonstrate that the applicant has carefully considered the practical execution of the project. Expected Outputs The proposal should identify expected research outputs. These may include: Academic publications Intellectual property Other significant research outputs Contribution to the Field and Required Infrastructure Applicants should explain how the research will contribute to their academic field. The proposal should also identify the infrastructure and research resources required for successful implementation. How Applications Are Evaluated Being eligible does not guarantee selection. The University of Pretoria uses institutional assessment criteria to evaluate and rank applications. Important assessment areas include the applicant s research track record, academic merit, strategic alignment and the quality of the host environment. Research Track Record Reviewers consider the candidate s research outputs and broader academic record. A strong research portfolio can therefore strengthen the application. Academic Merit The proposed research is assessed in terms of originality and feasibility. Applicants should demonstrate that their project represents meaningful scholarly work while also being achievable within the available fellowship period. Alignment with University of Pretoria Priorities The research should demonstrate alignment with the University s strategic research focus. Applicants should therefore investigate the relevant research environment and explain how their project fits within the University s broader research objectives. Host Environment The capacity of the host and the available research environment are also considered. This includes the host s ability to provide appropriate academic mentorship and research support. Co-Funding Does Not Guarantee Selection An important point for applicants is that a nomination or financial commitment does not automatically result in a fellowship award. Similarly, external funding availability does not guarantee an award. All applications remain subject to formal institutional eligibility, academic assessment, panel evaluation and available funding. Fellowship Governance and Post-Award Requirements Successful fellows must comply with the University s institutional policies throughout their fellowship. Ethics Approval Research involving regulated areas such as: Human participants Animals Sensitive or regulated data must obtain the required University of Pretoria ethics approval before the research begins. Applicants should consider ethics requirements during the planning stage rather than waiting until after receiving the fellowship. Publications and Research Outputs Fellows must comply with UP s institutional policies concerning publications and intellectual property. Publications arising from the fellowship must explicitly acknowledge the University of Pretoria and the Department of Research and Innovation . The University s standard intellectual property policies also apply. Immigration Requirements for International Fellows International candidates are responsible for obtaining the necessary South African immigration clearance before travelling to South Africa and completing registration. Applicants should therefore begin considering visa and immigration requirements early if they are successful. Official Award Confirmation Applicants should also understand that an informal communication, host nomination or indication of funding does not constitute a formal fellowship award. Only an official written University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship Award Letter constitutes formal confirmation of the fellowship. Important Dates for the University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 The most important date in the 2027 fellowship call is the application deadline. Final Application Deadline 30 October 2026 at 23:59 SAST The deadline is strict. Late applications will not be accepted under any circumstances. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit before the final day to avoid potential technical problems or system congestion. Panel Evaluation After applications close, submissions undergo institutional assessment by the relevant DRI Postdoctoral Fellowship Review Committee . The committee evaluates applications according to the programme s academic and institutional criteria. Award Outcomes Successful applicants will receive formal fellowship award letters following the institutional assessment process. Fellowship Commencement Successful fellows will begin their fellowship during the 2027 academic year , subject to the applicable onboarding, registration and institutional requirements. Why Researchers Should Consider the University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 The University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme provides an opportunity for early-career researchers to develop their academic careers within a major South African research institution. The programme is particularly relevant for researchers who: Completed their PhD within the required five-year period. Are 40 years old or younger. Have a strong research track record. Have a well-developed postdoctoral research proposal. Can identify a suitable University of Pretoria research host. Want to conduct research in a structured university environment. Are South African or international researchers seeking a postdoctoral opportunity in South Africa. The co-funding pathway is especially significant because the 2027 call prioritises applications supported by institutional host funding. Researchers who already have connections with appropriate UP academics should therefore begin discussions with potential hosts well before submitting their applications. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Applicants should avoid treating the fellowship application as simply a document-upload exercise. The research proposal, academic record and host environment all contribute to the assessment. Before submitting, applicants should: Confirm that they satisfy the five-year PhD requirement. Confirm that they meet the age requirement. Identify a suitable University of Pretoria research host. Discuss the research project with the proposed host. Determine whether the co-funding pathway is appropriate. Confirm the host s ability to provide the required financial contribution. Obtain the required UP Cost Centre information where applicable. Prepare a strong five-page research proposal. Update the CV and publications list. Obtain the required academic reference. Certify documents according to the applicable requirements. Confirm that all required PDFs are uploaded correctly. Check the application for missing information before submission. Submit well before the 30 October 2026 deadline. Contact Information Applicants who require clarification regarding the University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme can contact the Graduate Support Hub. Contact Person: Mpho Maithufi Email: mpho.maithufi@up.ac.za Institution: University of Pretoria Graduate Support Hub (GSH) University Website: University of Pretoria Application Deadline 30 October 2026 at 23:59 SAST Applicants should note that late submissions will not be accepted. The University of Pretoria Postdoctoral Fellowship Programme 2027 offers an important research opportunity for emerging scholars within five years of completing their PhD. Open to South African citizens, permanent residents and international candidates, the programme provides several funding pathways, including the priority UP Co-Funding track, which can provide a combined fellowship package of at least R250,000 per year . The fellowship is designed not only to provide financial support but also to strengthen research capacity, connect emerging scholars with University of Pretoria research leaders and contribute to the University s broader research priorities. Applicants should pay particular attention to the PhD eligibility window, age requirement, confirmed UP host requirement, research proposal, supporting documentation and co-funding requirements. Researchers interested in applying should begin preparing their documents and contacting potential University of Pretoria hosts as early as possible. With the application deadline set for 30 October 2026 at 23:59 SAST , applicants should ensure that their complete applications are submitted well before the closing time. title: JPMorganChase Corporate Analyst Development Program 2027: 9-Week Summer Internship in Bournemouth, UK
summary: The JPMorganChase 2027 Corporate Analyst Development Program (CADP) Summer Analyst Internship is now accepting applications from eligible students seeking to gain practical experience in analytics, project management, and process improvement within one of the world’s leading financial institutions. Based in Bournemouth, Dorset, United Kingdom , this nine-week summer internship provides students with an opportunity to work on meaningful projects, collaborate with professionals across the organization, develop transferable business skills, and gain exposure to how data, analytics, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies are used responsibly to support business decisions. The program is particularly suitable for students who enjoy solving problems, analyzing information, improving processes, working with teams, and turning ideas into practical results. Opportunity Overview The JPMorganChase Corporate Analyst Development Program is designed to expose Summer Analysts to the internal operations and business functions that support a global financial institution. During the nine-week internship, participants will contribute to projects that can influence real business outcomes. Rather than focusing on front-office client-facing work or software engineering, the program concentrates on broad business capabilities that can be applied across many professional environments. Participants will develop foundational experience in one of three main disciplines: Analytics Project Management Process Improvement The internship also provides exposure to senior stakeholders, different areas of JPMorganChase, and the ways in which modern technologies, including AI-enabled tools, can be responsibly incorporated into business processes and decision-making. About the JPMorganChase Corporate Analyst Development Program The Corporate Analyst Development Program is structured around the development of broad and transferable professional skills. Throughout the internship, Summer Analysts will be expected to contribute to projects, work with colleagues from different teams, analyze problems, communicate recommendations, and support initiatives that improve how the organization operates. The experience is designed for students who want to understand how large organizations function and who are interested in developing capabilities that can be useful across a wide range of careers. High-performing Summer Analysts may also have the opportunity to receive an offer to return to JPMorganChase for the full-time Corporate Analyst Development Program. The full-time program is a two-year rotational experience covering the three core disciplines of: Analytics Project Management Process Improvement This means the summer internship can potentially serve as a pathway toward longer-term professional development with JPMorganChase. What Will Interns Do? The internship provides practical experience across several areas of corporate functions. Participants may be involved in projects that require research, data analysis, coordination, communication, problem-solving, process evaluation, and implementation. 1. Analytics The Analytics track focuses on using information and data to generate useful insights that can support business decisions. Summer Analysts may be expected to: Explore data to identify trends, patterns, and opportunities. Analyze information to understand business challenges. Translate analytical findings into clear recommendations. Support decision-making through structured problem-solving. Use modern digital tools to improve the generation and interpretation of insights. Explore responsible applications of AI-enabled solutions. Present analytical findings in a way that can be understood and acted upon by stakeholders. Students interested in data, research, business analysis, statistics, technology, or evidence-based decision-making may find this area particularly relevant. 2. Project Management The Project Management discipline focuses on transforming business ideas and priorities into practical outcomes. Participants may: Support the delivery of projects aligned with business priorities. Coordinate activities across different teams. Help keep projects on schedule. Communicate project updates to stakeholders. Identify potential risks and challenges. Contribute to solving problems that emerge during project implementation. Adapt to changing priorities and business requirements. Work collaboratively with people at different levels of the organization. This discipline can be particularly valuable for students interested in leadership, operations, administration, project coordination, consulting, business management, or organizational development. 3. Process Improvement The Process Improvement discipline focuses on identifying inefficiencies and developing better ways of working. Participants may: Analyze existing workflows. title: Durham University Transformative Humanities PhD Studentships 2027: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity for Home and Overseas Students
summary: Durham University has announced a competitive funding opportunity for outstanding candidates interested in pursuing doctoral research within the field of Transformative Humanities . The university is offering up to eleven PhD Studentships for candidates beginning their doctoral programmes in October 2027 . The studentships are supported through the AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award together with support from Durham University s Faculty of Arts and Humanities and Faculty of Social Sciences . The scheme is intended to support doctoral research projects connected to Durham University s Transformative Humanities framework , with an emphasis on interdisciplinary research involving collaboration across academic departments. For prospective PhD students looking for substantial doctoral funding in the United Kingdom, this opportunity offers a combination of financial support, research development, additional funding opportunities, and access to training and placement resources. The application deadline for the scheme is noon UK time on 15 January 2027 , making early preparation particularly important for applicants who need to develop a research proposal, identify potential supervisors, prepare references, and complete the required application materials. Durham University Transformative Humanities PhD Studentships 2027 Durham University is inviting applications for up to eleven PhD Studentships in Transformative Humanities . Successful candidates will begin their PhD programmes in October 2027 and will undertake research projects connected to the university s Transformative Humanities framework. The programme is supported by both the AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award and Durham University s Faculties of Arts Humanities and Social Sciences . The interdisciplinary structure of the scheme is particularly important. Applicants are expected to develop projects that involve collaboration across academic departments, with supervision including participation from at least two departments . This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to prospective doctoral researchers whose research interests can connect different academic disciplines and contribute to broader discussions within the humanities and social sciences. What Does the PhD Studentship Cover? Each successful award provides several forms of financial and professional support throughout the doctoral programme. According to Durham University, each studentship includes: A tuition fee waiver A stipend for 3.5 years for full-time study A stipend for 7 years for part-time study Stipend funding at the level set by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) Additional funding opportunities Access to training resources Access to placement resources The combination of tuition support and a doctoral stipend can significantly reduce the financial burden associated with undertaking a PhD. The programme also goes beyond tuition and living-cost support by providing access to training and placement resources designed to support researchers during their doctoral studies. How Many PhD Studentships Are Available? Durham University is offering up to eleven studentships through this scheme. The funding is divided between home and overseas applicants: Up to nine awards are available to home students. Up to two awards are available to overseas students. Home awards cover tuition fees at the home-student level. Overseas awards cover tuition fees at the overseas-student level. This means the competition is open to both home and international applicants, although the number of awards available to overseas candidates is limited to up to two. Prospective international applicants should therefore pay particular attention to the funding structure when preparing their applications. What Is Transformative Humanities Research? The studentships are specifically connected to Durham University s Transformative Humanities framework . Applicants are expected to propose research projects that relate to the themes of this framework. This means that having a strong research idea alone is not sufficient; applicants also need to demonstrate how their proposed doctoral research connects with the Transformative Humanities focus and fits within Durham University s academic environment. The application requirements specifically ask candidates to explain: Their research questions The context of their research Their intended approach Their research methods The relevance of their proposed project to Transformative Humanities The fit between their proposed project and Durham University These requirements demonstrate that the university is looking for applicants with clearly developed and academically grounded research proposals. Interdisciplinary Research Is a Key Requirement One of the most important characteristics of the Durham University Transformative Humanities PhD Studentships is the emphasis on cross-disciplinary supervision . Applicants must be accepted onto a PhD programme at Durham University with a supervisory team led by the Faculty of Arts Humanities or the Faculty of Social Sciences. In addition, supervision must involve collaboration across at least two departments . This interdisciplinary requirement means prospective applicants should think carefully about how their research connects different areas of academic expertise. For example, a research project may need to demonstrate connections between different fields within the humanities and social sciences, depending on the subject and proposed research questions. Applicants should therefore consider not only their research topic but also which academic departments and potential supervisors would be best positioned to support the project. Who Can Be Considered for the Studentship? The scheme is specifically intended for applicants who are accepted as PhD students at Durham University . The university states that only PhD students accepted to Durham University with a supervisory team led by Arts Humanities or Social Sciences will be considered for the scheme. The competition is open to: Home students Overseas students However, applicants must satisfy the university s PhD admission requirements in addition to being considered for the studentship. Applicants should therefore review the relevant Durham University PhD programme requirements for their proposed subject before applying. This is an important part of preparing a strong application. A potential supervisor can help an applicant determine whether: Their proposed research fits the department s expertise. The project is suitable for doctoral-level research. The proposed methodology is appropriate. The research connects with Transformative Humanities. The university has the academic expertise needed to support the project. The project could involve suitable collaboration between departments. Because the studentship requires supervision involving at least two departments, applicants should pay particular attention to the interdisciplinary structure of their proposed supervisory team. Recommended Application Preparation Prospective applicants should begin preparing well before the January deadline. A useful preparation process can include the following steps: 1. Develop a Strong Research Idea Applicants should identify a research problem or question that can support a substantial doctoral project. The proposed research should have clearly defined research questions and a strong academic context. 2. Explore Durham University s Research Expertise Applicants should investigate the relevant departments, academics, and research areas at Durham University. The purpose is to determine where their proposed research fits within the university. 3. Identify Potential Supervisors Applicants should identify potential supervisors whose academic expertise aligns with their proposed research. Durham University specifically recommends contacting potential supervisors to discuss the project before applying. 4. Consider the Interdisciplinary Requirement Applicants should determine how their research could involve at least two departments. This should be reflected naturally in the research design rather than added simply to satisfy a formal requirement. 5. Prepare the Research Proposal The research proposal is one of the central components of the application. The proposal must be no longer than 1,000 words , including footnotes but excluding the bibliography, if applicable. Prepare the CV Applicants must submit a CV with a maximum length of two pages . The CV should present the applicant s academic and relevant professional background clearly and efficiently. 7. Arrange Two Referees Applicants must provide the contact details of two referees . The online application system provides information about submitting reference letters. Applicants should therefore contact their referees early rather than waiting until immediately before the deadline. 8. After submitting the form, applicants receive a code that should be retained as proof of submission. 9. Submit the PhD Application Applications should be submitted to the PhD programme of the lead supervisor s department through Durham University s online application system. How to Indicate That You Want to Be Considered for the Studentship Applicants need to identify their interest in the Transformative Humanities studentship within the funding section of their PhD application. Under Scholarship details, applicants should type: Transformative Humanities Applicants who also want to be considered for other funding schemes should list those schemes as well. This step is important because simply applying for a Durham University PhD does not automatically communicate an applicant s intention to be considered for this particular funding scheme. Required Application Documents Applicants should prepare the following materials for the application: Research Proposal A research proposal of no more than 1,000 words , including footnotes but excluding the bibliography if applicable. The proposal should cover: Research questions Research context Approach Methods Relevance to Transformative Humanities Fit with Durham University Curriculum Vitae A CV of no more than two pages . Equal Opportunities Monitoring Form Applicants must complete the required monitoring form and retain the submission code they receive afterward as proof of completion. Two Referees Applicants must provide the contact details of two referees. The online application system will provide further instructions regarding reference letters. title: Institute for Youth in Policy Public Policy Fellowship 2027
summary: The Institute for Youth in Policy (YIP) Public Policy Fellowship 2027 is a two-month development program designed for young people interested in public policy, civic engagement, social impact, political issues, and innovative solutions to major social, economic, and environmental challenges. The fellowship provides participants with an opportunity to collaborate with other emerging leaders, engage with policy professionals and community stakeholders, strengthen their policy analysis and communication abilities, and develop practical projects addressing real-world issues. Rather than being limited to classroom-style learning, the program combines workshops, discussions, debates, mentorship, speaker sessions, collaborative policy work, and an individual capstone project. Through these activities, fellows are encouraged to examine policy challenges from personal, local, and global perspectives while developing the skills needed to contribute to meaningful change. The program has already built a significant alumni network, with more than 1,500 fellows graduating , more than 300 fellow capstones published , and more than 3.2 million views of fellows capstone projects . According to YIP, approximately 80% of its leadership began through the Fellowship , while the program has historically maintained an average acceptance rate of approximately 5–8% . About the Institute for Youth in Policy Public Policy Fellowship The Public Policy Fellowship is designed for young, emerging leaders who want to understand how public policy is developed and how individuals can participate in creating positive social, political, economic, and environmental change. During the program, fellows work alongside peers, YIP department executives, political and educational leaders, mentors, and community stakeholders. These interactions allow participants to examine contemporary policy challenges while developing solutions through different forms of research, communication, collaboration, and project development. The fellowship also emphasizes the practical side of policy work. Participants are expected not simply to discuss problems but to investigate issues, think critically about possible solutions, communicate their ideas effectively, and ultimately develop an original capstone project. The program can therefore be particularly valuable for students who are considering future involvement in areas such as public policy, government, international affairs, civic engagement, advocacy, education, technology policy, social innovation, community development, or related fields. What Does the Public Policy Fellowship Offer? The fellowship provides a combination of professional development, policy education, collaborative work, mentorship, and practical project experience. Participants have opportunities to develop skills in several important areas, including: Policy analysis: Fellows learn to examine public policy issues and consider potential solutions. Policy development: Participants gain experience thinking about how policies can be designed and improved. Project management: Fellows develop experience planning and completing projects within a defined period. Communication: The program helps participants strengthen their ability to communicate complex ideas effectively. Teamwork: Fellows collaborate with other young leaders on policy-related activities. Debate and discussion: Participants engage in discussions and debates surrounding important policy issues. Problem-solving: Fellows are encouraged to develop innovative responses to contemporary challenges. Nonpartisan thinking: The program emphasizes examining policy issues through a broader and analytical perspective. Public speaking and articulation: Participants have opportunities to present their ideas and policy work. Research and writing: Fellows work on original policy-related written projects. Leadership development: The fellowship can help young participants develop the skills and confidence needed for future leadership opportunities. Key Policy Areas Covered by the Fellowship The fellowship is designed to expose participants to a broad range of policy and civic issues rather than restricting them to one specific field. The program highlights areas such as: Social Change Fellows can explore policies and initiatives intended to improve communities and address social challenges. This encourages participants to consider how institutions, organizations, and individuals can work together to create positive social outcomes. Urban Renewal Urban development and renewal can involve questions surrounding infrastructure, housing, transportation, public services, community development, and the long-term sustainability of cities. The fellowship provides an opportunity for young leaders to consider how policy can contribute to more effective and inclusive urban development. Public Policy Reform Participants can examine existing policies, identify challenges, and consider innovative approaches to policy reform. This gives fellows an opportunity to think critically about how government policies can respond to changing social and economic conditions. SMART Infrastructure and Technology Technology increasingly influences how governments and communities operate. The fellowship highlights SMART infrastructure and technology initiatives as areas where emerging leaders can explore innovative approaches to modern social and policy challenges. This can be particularly relevant for students interested in the relationship between technology, government, infrastructure, and public services. Education Education policy is another area that participants may explore. Fellows can examine challenges affecting education systems and consider potential approaches for improving educational access, quality, and outcomes. A Practical and Collaborative Fellowship Experience One of the distinguishing features of the YIP Fellowship is its emphasis on collaboration. Fellows are not expected to learn entirely independently. Throughout the program, participants interact with their peers and mentors while engaging with policy-related discussions, workshops, seminars, debates, and guest speakers. This collaborative environment gives participants the opportunity to encounter different perspectives and learn how other young people approach social and policy challenges. The fellowship also encourages participants to look at policy issues from several different levels: Personal level – considering how policies and social issues affect individuals. Local level – examining challenges within communities and cities. Global level – understanding how policy challenges connect to broader international issues. This approach can help fellows develop a more comprehensive understanding of policy and civic problems. Capstone Project: Turning Ideas Into Action A major component of the Public Policy Fellowship is the individual capstone project . Throughout the fellowship, participants develop an original project connected to an issue of interest. The capstone gives fellows an opportunity to move beyond theoretical discussions and demonstrate their ability to investigate an issue and develop a meaningful response. The capstone process extends from approximately the second week of the fellowship through the end of the program. Fellows also present their work as part of the fellowship experience. This can become a valuable addition to a participant s academic or professional portfolio because it demonstrates initiative, research ability, policy thinking, project development, and communication skills. YIP also publishes fellow capstones, meaning successful projects can receive visibility beyond the fellowship itself. According to the organization, more than 300 fellows capstones have been published , with those projects receiving more than 3.2 million views . Policy Brief and Collaborative Work In addition to the individual capstone project, fellows work with their peers to develop an original policy brief and present it. This collaborative assignment provides practical experience in researching a policy issue, developing an argument, working with a team, producing written policy material, and presenting recommendations. Such experience can be useful for students who are interested in future careers involving: Government Public policy International organizations Nonprofit organizations Civic organizations Advocacy Research Political analysis Community development Public administration Social innovation Workshops, Seminars and Discussions The fellowship uses a variety of educational formats rather than relying on a single teaching method. Participants may take part in: Interactive workshops Policy seminars Thought-provoking debates Group discussions Guest speaker sessions Mentorship activities Collaborative projects Policy writing Presentations Capstone development These activities are designed to help fellows strengthen both their understanding of policy and their ability to communicate and apply that knowledge. Fellowship Speaker Sessions Speaker events are described by YIP as one of the foundational components of the fellowship. The organization aims to provide two speaker sessions per cohort , with experts representing different policy areas. The purpose is to expose fellows to professionals with diverse experiences and perspectives on civic and policy issues. YIP states that decisions for the Winter 2027 cohort will be released on January 6, 2027 . Applications close at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Standard Time on the applicable deadline date . Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final minutes to submit their applications, particularly because application systems and internet connectivity can sometimes cause unexpected delays. Applicants interested in later cohorts should check the official fellowship page and application form for the applicable deadlines. How Much Time Does the Fellowship Require? The fellowship was designed with students and young people who have busy schedules in mind. Rather than requiring participants to attend activities throughout every weekday, the program has structured weekly synchronous meetings. According to YIP, fellows have two mandatory weekly synchronous meetings : Wednesdays at 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time Saturdays at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time The program also includes asynchronous work and the individual capstone project. YIP reports that most fellows spend approximately 4–6 hours per week on the fellowship, including synchronous meetings and asynchronous activities. This structure allows students to participate while continuing with their academic responsibilities and other commitments. However, prospective applicants should carefully convert the meeting times to their own local time zones before applying. How the Application Process Works The application process is designed to be relatively straightforward. The general process involves three main stages: 1. Explore the Program Before applying, prospective fellows are encouraged to learn more about the fellowship, including previous fellow profiles and published capstone projects. Reviewing previous projects can help applicants understand the type of work fellows have completed and the kind of policy interests represented within the program. 2. Submit the Application Applicants complete the fellowship application form and provide the information requested by YIP. Because the fellowship has historically reported an average acceptance rate of approximately 5–8% , applicants should take the application seriously and clearly communicate their interests, experiences, motivation, and commitment to policy and civic engagement. 3. Receive the Decision YIP publishes decision dates on its website and sends application results to applicants by email. Applicants should therefore monitor the email address used during the application process after submitting their application. What Happens During the Fellowship? After qualified applicants are selected, fellows begin an immersive development experience focused on personal, professional, and political growth. The fellowship combines several elements: Seminars to introduce and explore important policy concepts. Debates to encourage critical thinking and effective articulation. Interactive workshops to develop practical skills. Guest speaker sessions to expose fellows to experienced policy professionals. Peer collaboration to develop teamwork and communication skills. Policy brief development to provide experience in policy writing. Individual capstone development to allow fellows to pursue an original policy project. Presentations to strengthen communication and public-speaking abilities. Mentorship and guidance throughout the fellowship. YIP describes the experience as one in which participants outcomes depend significantly on the effort they put into the program. What Skills Can Participants Gain? The Public Policy Fellowship can provide participants with a broad collection of transferable skills. Policy and Research Skills Participants develop greater familiarity with policy analysis, research, policy development, and identifying potential solutions to complex issues. Leadership Skills By working with peers, mentors, and professionals, fellows can develop leadership capabilities and learn how to contribute to collaborative initiatives. Communication Skills Policy professionals must be able to communicate complicated ideas clearly. Through discussions, debates, presentations, and written projects, fellows can strengthen this ability. Teamwork Skills The collaborative nature of the fellowship gives participants experience working with people who may have different backgrounds, interests, and approaches. Project Management Skills The capstone project provides practical experience in taking an idea from development through completion. Problem-Solving Skills The program encourages participants to investigate real-world challenges and consider innovative solutions rather than simply identifying problems. Professional Networking Interaction with fellow participants, mentors, department executives, guest speakers, political leaders, educational leaders, and community stakeholders can help participants expand their professional networks. What Happens After Completing the Fellowship? The benefits of the program can continue after the fellowship ends. YIP states that fellows receive priority consideration and direct access to the organization s C-suite and senior vice presidents for hiring and other positions . The organization also maintains a priority hiring pipeline for fellowship graduates. Additionally, fellows capstone projects can be published on the YIP website, providing participants with a public record of their work. For students planning careers in policy, civic engagement, research, advocacy, or related areas, this combination of fellowship experience, published work, networking, and potential organizational opportunities can be particularly valuable. Why the Public Policy Fellowship May Be Valuable for Students The fellowship can be useful for students who want to develop experience beyond their regular academic coursework. University courses can provide theoretical knowledge, but professional development programs can give students opportunities to practice communication, collaboration, research, project management, and problem-solving in a structured environment. The YIP Fellowship combines these elements with a focus on public policy and social impact. A participant can potentially finish the program with: Fellowship experience An original capstone project Policy-writing experience Presentation experience Collaborative project experience Exposure to policy professionals Mentorship experience A broader professional network A stronger understanding of civic engagement A portfolio project that can be shared with future academic or professional opportunities Important Things Applicants Should Know Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully consider several aspects of the program. Check the Eligibility Requirements Applicants should confirm that they meet YIP s age, education, and geographic eligibility requirements before submitting an application. The eligibility rules are particularly important because the program currently has restrictions regarding international applicants. Consider the Meeting Times The two required weekly meetings are scheduled according to U.S. time zones. Applicants living outside those time zones should carefully determine whether they can consistently attend the required sessions. Prepare for the Capstone The capstone is not simply an optional activity. It is a central part of the fellowship experience. Applicants should therefore be prepared to dedicate time to researching an issue, developing an original project, and eventually presenting their work. Understand the Competitive Nature of the Program With an average historical acceptance rate of approximately 5–8%, applicants should not assume that meeting the basic requirements guarantees selection. A strong application should clearly communicate the applicant s interests, experiences, motivation, and potential contribution to the fellowship. How to Apply for the Public Policy Fellowship Applicants interested in the program should use the official Institute for Youth in Policy application form. The organization encourages prospective fellows to explore previous fellow profiles and capstone projects before applying. Applications are submitted through the fellowship application form, and applicants receive results by email after the selection process. The two-month program goes beyond traditional learning by combining policy discussions, interactive workshops, debates, professional speaker sessions, peer collaboration, mentorship, policy writing, and practical project development. One of its most significant components is the individual capstone project, which allows fellows to turn a policy interest into an original piece of work that can potentially become part of their professional portfolio. The fellowship also provides participants with opportunities to interact with other emerging leaders and professionals from different areas of public policy and civic engagement. For students who are serious about developing communication, policy analysis, teamwork, project management, research, and leadership skills, these experiences can provide useful preparation for future academic and professional opportunities. Because the fellowship is competitive and has historically reported an acceptance rate of approximately 5–8%, interested applicants should review the eligibility requirements carefully, prepare a thoughtful application, and submit it before the deadline.
